check: RoadWeaver interop gate will pass on the real machine
why: The mod refuses to initialise the soft-dependency bridge unless the loaded RoadWeaver jar matches an allowlisted SHA. If it did not match, the wall would fail to initialise on the user's client - a real-machine failure that no amount of local testing would show.
interpretation: The exact jar that will load on the real machine carries the allowlisted SHA and exposes every interop entry point the adapter calls, so the bridge initialises rather than refusing.
falseAlarmRecorded: A first listing reported the localisation pack as sharing the main jar's SHA. That was a shell artefact: a failed Get-FileHash left the previous loop's variable in place. Re-read per file, the two differ (6395395 vs 47813 bytes), as they must.
